items.finding: The timing test takes the best of three runs over the SAME 1 MB string, so an implementation that memoizes on the payload makes runs 2 and 3 free and reports 0.0000 s/MB while its real first-call cost is unchanged. An adversarial validator proved this with two variants, one of them keyed on a colliding fingerprint that actually loses detection. The test shape (two 1 MB prompts, best of three) is pinned verbatim by the PRD and the design doc, so it was NOT changed. A human should decide whether to re-spec the test to time a fresh input per repetition.

items.finding: The 0.3 s/MB bound sits inside the noise band of a wall-clock measurement on this machine. Measured on byte-identical code at HEAD: 0.46/0.34 (orchestrator), 0.36/0.30 and 0.43/0.36 (test author), then 0.33/0.28 and 0.17/0.13 (adversarial validator, verdict flipped from fail to pass). The PRD Risks section anticipates this and says a flake means the bound, not the code, needs review - which is a human decision, so the bound was left at the contracted 0.3.

items.finding: The non-ASCII path of _normalize keeps its per-character unicodedata.category loop (_fold_run), now behind an extra regex pass, so the measured speedup applies to pure-ASCII prompts only. A prompt padded with combining marks or fullwidth text should get none of it, and nothing bounds that case: the contracted timing test uses two pure-ASCII strings. Pat (per-task review) could not measure it. Suggested fix: a second timing test over a 1 MB non-ASCII string at the same bound, and if it fails, a str.translate table for the dropped and Pd categories rather than a looser bound.

items.finding: Pat raised seven LOW findings on hooks/test_read_input.py, none CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM, so per the step-5.7 ladder they were noted and not fixed in-task. Three are claims in the new module that are factually overstated and worth correcting: (1) the U+FFFD case comment says tool_name=Skill makes the hooks actually engage, but guard_phase_delegation acts on Agent, guard_push_on_critical on Bash and enforce_prd_location on file writes, so a Skill payload short-circuits most of them and those matrix cells add little beyond the empty-stdin cases - fix the claim or give each hook a payload it acts on; (2) the harness passes the REAL Path.home() as HOME while the comment says the tmp_path cwd stops a hook reaching the real repo, so a hook writing under ~ would still hit the real home - set HOME to the tmp cwd; (3) REPLACEMENT is written as a literal U+FFFD character rather than the escape \ufffd, which is invisible-prone in source. Two more: the splice test asserts only returncode==2 without checking it is the SAME deny the clean payload produces, so any other exit-2 path would pass; and the module docstring repeats itself. Pat also DISMISSED the slop pass claim that the fixture self-check assert is tautological, with a correct argument: it guards fixture drift, because if the spliced word ever left the fixture the replace would be a no-op and the returncode assertion would pass vacuously.

items.question: Task 9 requires the live replay to exit 0, but the design-doc exit rule makes that unreachable.
items.detail: The contract says exit 1 when ANY per-task/agoge/reviewer record is refused, AND separately when a pinned deny id is allowed. The pinned deny id toolu_01Ku4TbcQoeik6ZLf5XkkAuD (general-purpose, "Resume work phase for PRD 00242, task 1 onward") buckets as per-task because its description matches \btask\s+1\b, and it MUST be refused. So its correct refusal trips the first clause: exit 1 is forced no matter what the predicate does. Only three resolutions exist and the task forbids two of them (change buckets, change the deny list); the third is to exempt pinned-deny ids from the bucket-refusal clause, which cannot mask a regression (an ALLOWED pinned id still fails, a refused non-pinned per-task record still fails). Left unapplied: it is a design-doc change, not an implementor call. Verbatim contract kept, exit 1 recorded as evidence, same handling as task 7s unreachable fails-at-base criterion.
items.assumption: Replay CLI shipped verbatim to contract; exit 1 reported as a finding rather than engineered away.

items.question: The replay found six legitimate per-task dispatches the guard refuses, all because a phase name sits inside a QUOTED run.
items.detail: Measured against 1172 deduped dispatches (800 per-task): 7 per-task refusals. One is the pinned deny id (correct). The other six, with the span the guard quoted: (1) toolu_015DM18ubZLJZbA65ozvuw8c, no subagent_type, span "e-invokes `/autopilot:work`, w" - narrative prose about what re-invokes the skill. (2) toolu_013NAWvgMnP4WatpZDVyiNAa, (3) toolu_01DAQSaS3uAph2VZnfn5NC9d, (4) toolu_019nCz3WRsAZSwdaHb9itXiT, general-purpose, spans "d reports `design-solution: <p", ".assertIn(\"design-solution: <p", "ine reads `design-solution: <p" - a log-line FORMAT quoted as expected test output. (5) toolu_013ePUKbLDE7DLnbnGmgszzR, general-purpose, span "parse and plan-tasks) looks fo" - paren aside. (6) toolu_011UqbqFtUDPuSeCiLLgMvEg, autopilot:worker-opus, span "`Run the work phase for PRD 0" - this PRDs own trigger string quoted as test data, strong-anchored, and the one the session brief already records as costing a denied dispatch. Common shape: an open wrapper (backtick, double quote, paren) opens BEFORE the name and closes AFTER more text, so the name is a citation rather than the thing to run. The guard treats a wrapper as neutral: _candidates consumes a close only when it sits immediately after the name, so a longer quoted run leaves the bare name weakly anchored by the following punctuation. Five of the six also depend on per_task being false because the historical dispatch used general-purpose or no type. NOT fixed in task 9: a quoted-citation concept is a new anchoring rule in a predicate whose shape is pinned verbatim by the design doc and covered by 564 tests across three suites, so it is a design decision, not an implementor rewrite. Fixing all six would still not reach exit 0 (see the contract-conflict record), so no partial fix buys the stated goal either.
items.assumption: Predicate left exactly as tasks 5 and 6 shipped it; the six spans recorded for the design-level call.
